facts.statement: The researchers built a detailed map of the human basal ganglia by combining two specific sequencing technologies on tissue from four healthy people.

facts.statement: Specific types of neurons and non-neuronal cells showed unique molecular and location patterns that varied depending on which part of the basal ganglia they were in.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The location of RNA inside individual cells helped reveal the physical size of the cell bodies and the direction of their connections within the brain's pathways.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Certain groups of support cells were found mostly at the edges between two brain zones, while a specific type of interneuron was found only inside one of those zones.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Comparing human data with other primates showed that some brain structures are organized similarly across species, while other details are unique to humans.
